frames.title: Reading · An academic passage with summary

blocks.title: Abstract: Do Thought Experiments Move Us?
paras: This (fictional) study **investigates** whether **thought experiments** alter moral judgment. **Participants** (N = 240) **read** one of two versions of a classic dilemma, **differing only in** wording: *killing* versus *letting die*. **Judgements** were **recorded** on a seven-point scale.

**Results** show that wording **significantly shifted** ratings: participants **who read** “kill” rated the act **more severely** than those who read “let die”, **even though** the outcomes **were identical**. **This pattern is consistent with** the view that intuitions are **sensitive to framing**.

**Caution is warranted**: the sample **consisted solely of** university students, and **no claim** about philosophers’ **expert intuitions** can be made. **Replication** with **broader samples** is needed.

items.q: The two versions differed only in wording.
The outcomes in the two versions were different.
The study speaks about expert philosophers.
items.why: no claim about philosophers can be made.

body: **Be consistent with** — ser compatível com
**Call for caution** — pedir cautela
**Bear out** — confirmar
**Lend support to** — dar respaldo a
**Lead to the conclusion** — levar à conclusão
**Cast doubt on** — lançar dúvida sobre
**Take into account** — levar em conta
**Account for** — explicar
**Give rise to** — dar origem a
**Be at odds with** — estar em desacordo com
**Did the wording change the ratings?** — A redação mudou as notas?
**Even though the outcomes were identical?** — Mesmo com resultados idênticos?
**Yes, which suggests sensitivity to framing.** — Sim, o que sugere sensibilidade ao enquadramento.

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence abstract about a fictional study of moral judgment, with aim, method, result and limitation.
blocks.model: This study investigates whether wording alters moral judgment. Participants read one of two versions of a short dilemma, differing only in a verb. Results show that the stronger verb produced harsher ratings, even though outcomes were identical. This is consistent with sensitivity to framing. Caution is warranted, as the sample consisted solely of students. Replication is needed.

items.why: **thought experiment study** = estudo com experimento mental.

items.q: What does “doing versus allowing harm” mean?
items.why: **doing versus allowing harm** = causar versus permitir dano.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.

Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
